title: The trigger of the step, the home of the recommendation and the mapping of the five route words to a closed list have no single source
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E3-027, Acceptance criteria AC1, Data, Endpoints, Screen and states); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.10.1, A2.10.2, A2.10.3.1, A2.10.3.3, A2.10.4.1, A2.10.4.4); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T3.1, T3.2, T4, T5.3, appendix T-A.1); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-DIS-08, R-DIS-14, R-DIS-19); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (feature row FEAT-AST-10, runs unattended); _work/msr/context/S5.md (ownership rows of S5, one event, one job, one workflow; the connection matrix row S5)
section: APP s1 Story; s2 Business rationale; s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 1 to 8; s7 AC1; s8 BR6, BR7, BR10; s9; s11 Data; s12.1; s12.3; s12.4; s13 Solution plan; s19 Out of scope; CON s2, s7 AC6, s11 Data, s12.3, s12.4
description: Legacy AC1 states the trigger only as When its trigger arrives. FSD S5 A2.10.2 names it as a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer while A2.10.4.4 declares no background event, TSD S5 T5.3 declares one published event (AssetTakenOn) and no consumed event, and R-DIS-19 gives the step a state and an event (ASSET_HELD, READY_TO_SELL) with a two-working-day target. The two release rules R-DIS-14 and R-DIS-08 belong to the same machine and are carried by the same stage. The recommendation itself has no home: no source gives a recommendation table, a route column or a return column on asset, listing or asset_sale, and no source names an event that carries it, so it is persisted as the decision record of DP-03 plus the case state on rwb-case. The five route words of the criterion have no closed list: LOV-SALE-CHANNEL gives DUTCH_AUCTION, BROKER, DIRECT, LED_AUCTION and RAMC and no buy-back or rental value, while TSD S5 T4 carries the states ROUTE_APPROVED_BUYBACK and RENTAL_ACTIVE and none of ROUTE_APPROVED_AUCTION or ROUTE_APPROVED_RAMC is a list value. Architecture v5 slide 13 puts an E in the S5 row under S4 with no event named, so the possession fact of R-DIS-14 has no named event either.
evidence: FSD S5 v3 A2.10.2 step 1 reads Receives its trigger: a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer, and A2.10.4.4 is the row None, No background event; A2.10.3.3 gives None; runs unattended as the primary role with the sale officer as also-user; the legacy story AC1 reads Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place / When its trigger arrives; TSD S5 v2 T4 gives R-DIS-19 ASSET_HELD READY_TO_SELL ROUTE_RECOMMENDED and R-DIS-14 and R-DIS-08 to ASSET_HELD, T3.1 gives asset, listing and asset_sale with no recommendation or return column, and T3.2 gives LOV-SALE-CHANNEL as DUTCH_AUCTION, BROKER, DIRECT, LED_AUCTION, RAMC, LOV-HOLDING as HELD, LISTED, UNDER_OFFER, SOLD, TRANSFERRED, RENTED and no LOV for a route word; T5.3 lists one published event, AssetTakenOn; the context pack lists one event (EV-22), one job (JOB-19) and one workflow, and its connection matrix row S5 carries E under S4 with no event name; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DIS-08, R-DIS-14 and R-DIS-19 carry the five route words in the action text of R-DIS-19 and no list identifier.
area: Workflow and data model, S5 rwb-asset with P3 rwb-case and P7 rwb-decision
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the P3 rwb-case owner and the P7 rwb-decision owner
proposed: Keep the metadata and dependency rows as the plan gives them, start the step from the case signal the parent workflow forwards for the three states, persist the recommendation as the local decision record plus the case move, hold the five route words as reference data with their list mapping, and let step D1 decide whether a recommendation or return field is added by the DB story of this service.

title: The five consumed rows are class C in fact while both metadata rows carry None, the service holds no v_ace_* grant, and the asset table is absent from the ownership list
source: _work/msr/context/S5.md (service row, ownership rows of S5 with two tables, six REST operations, one event, one job and one workflow; naming and shared platform rules; the connection matrix row S5); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E3-027, Data table and permission table); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.10.2 Integration points, A2.10.3.1, A2.10.3.3); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T3.1, T5.2, appendix T-A.1); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-DIS-08, R-DIS-14, R-DIS-19)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 2 and 3; s7 AC1 to AC3; s8 BR3, BR4; s10 Authority; s11 Data; s12.2; s12.7; s12.8; s13 Solution plan; s19; CON s3; s7 AC3 and AC5; s11 Data; s12.2; s12.8
description: The step cannot run without five facts it does not own: the ACE asset fact, the COLLINS economics, the case state, the case move and the DISPOSAL package. The legacy data table names v_ace_npa_asset and recovery_case, the FSD names v_ace_score for the economics, and Architecture v5 keeps the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views read only by rwb-source-data, so neither view can be read here and both arrive on the owner's contracts. No source names the operations: the rwb-source-data data-product reads, the rwb-case case-move answer and the rwb-decision package read all carry the placeholder. The plan gives both slices empty C, I and X lists, so the five rows are contract dependencies in fact and are built against the published documents and the fakes on Day 1. R-DIS-19 also names Agent Runtime in its Systems column, which is P10 rwb-agent and DP-20, and neither the pattern set nor the C row of this key carries it. The Ownership Map gives S5 two tables, asset_sale and listing, and no asset row, while three sources give asset to S5, so the row is declared from the sources and the absence is recorded.
evidence: The legacy Data table of RWB-E3-027 lists recovery_case, v_ace_npa_asset, decision_log_entry and rule_row; FSD S5 v3 A2.10.2 reads Integration points: Workbench, ACE (COLLINS scores ingested by ACE; v_ace_score); Architecture v5 slides 29, 37 and 45 keep the recovery.v_ace_* views read only by rwb-source-data; TSD S5 v2 T5.2 sends the case to P3 and the decision log to P7 through published interfaces and appendix T-A.1 lists no operation of rwb-source-data, rwb-case or rwb-decision; the context pack lists asset_sale and listing as S5 tables with no asset row and gives the service one event, one job and one workflow; both plan slices of RWB-E3-027 carry empty C, I and X lists; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 row R-DIS-19 names Agent Runtime and COLLINS as its systems.
area: Contract and integration, S5 rwb-asset with P1 rwb-source-data, P3 rwb-case, P7 rwb-decision and P10 rwb-agent
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the solution architect and the P1, P3, P7 and P10 owners
proposed: Treat the five consumed rows as class C in fact and build both slices against their published documents and fakes on Day 1, keep the metadata C row as the plan gives it, declare the asset row from Architecture v5 slides 19 and 41 and TSD S5 T3.1, and let step D1 decide whether the five rows and a P10 agent row are added to the plan.

title: The legacy key carries no requirement id in the story master and the module requirement set has none for the route recommendation
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E3-027, metadata table with no Requirement row); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (both slices of RWB-E3-027, reqs list empty); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (requirements served, REQ-S5-001 to REQ-S5-010); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T8)
section: APP s18 Traceability; the reqs key of both fragments; CON s18 Traceability
description: The traceability of the two stories needs a sourced requirement. The story master of RWB-E3-027 carries no requirement id, both plan slices carry an empty reqs list, and the ten requirements of the module name the asset record, the stock balance, the re-appraisal, the prices, the listings, the rounds, the below-floor signature, the title transfer, the proceeds and the RAMC, buy-back and rental approvals, and none names the route recommendation itself. The nearest requirements are REQ-S5-004, whose pricing step consumes this recommendation, and REQ-S5-010, whose three routes this recommendation ranks, so both are traced as context and the empty list is recorded rather than filled with an invented identifier.
evidence: The metadata table of RWB-E3-027 gives Epic, Module, Feature, Process, Priority, Depends on and Decision only; the plan rows of RWB-S5-E3027-APP and RWB-S5-E3027-CON carry reqs as an empty list; FSD S5 requirements served lists REQ-S5-001 to REQ-S5-010 with REQ-S5-004 A start price and a floor price are proposed for every asset and REQ-S5-010 A transfer to the asset management company, a buy-back and a rental each follow a recorded approval, and no requirement for FEAT-AST-10; TSD S5 T8 maps REQ-S5-001 to REQ-S5-010 to FEAT-AST-01 and FEAT-AST-08 only.
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the business analyst
proposed: Trace both slices to FEAT-AST-10 and name REQ-S5-004 and REQ-S5-010 as the consuming and ranking requirements, and let step D1 decide whether the plan reqs list of the two slices is updated or a requirement is written for FEAT-AST-10.

title: No source names an operation, an event or a representation for the disposal-route recommendation, so the element and its property are design names of the baseline
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E3-027, Acceptance criteria, Endpoints); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.10.2, A2.10.3.3, A2.10.4.1); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T2, T4, T5.3, appendix T-A.1, T-A.2); Recovery Workbench API Specification v4 (asset operations); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 (slide 19 OUT, slide 43 event 22); _work/msr/context/S5.md (six REST operations, one event)
section: CON s1 Story; s2 Business rationale; s4 Flow steps 1 to 3; s7 AC1 and AC6; s8 BR1; s11 Data; s12.1; s12.3; s12.4; s12.8; s13 Solution plan; s17 Guardrails; s19 Out of scope
description: The recommendation has no surface of its own in any source. TSD S5 T-A.1 lists five operations for the module and none of them recommends a route; the legacy Endpoints table lists the two asset reads only; T5.3 gives one published event, AssetTakenOn, and Architecture v5 slide 43 lists event 22 as AssetTakenOn with rwb-case and rwb-payment as consumers; the FSD says the feature runs unattended and names no caller. The result a person sees on SCR-22 therefore has to be carried by an element of the existing reads, and the element name, its property name and its sub-shape are design choices. The baseline declares them additively within major version 1, and the risk is a drift between this element and the pricing story that consumes it, which is why the additive rule, the drift test and the absence tests are the acceptance criteria of the baseline.
evidence: TSD S5 v2 appendix T-A.1 lists API-S5-001 to API-S5-005 as GET /assets, GET /assets/{assetId}, POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations, POST /assets/{assetId}/listings and POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds, with no route or recommendation operation; T5.3 gives AssetTakenOn as the only published event and no consumed event; FSD S5 v3 A2.10.3.3 gives None; runs unattended and A2.10.2 gives three system steps with no caller; the legacy Endpoints table gives the two reads with right R only; Architecture v5 slide 43 row 22 gives event 22 AssetTakenOn with rwb-case and rwb-payment; the context pack gives the service six REST operations and one event.
area: Contract, S5 rwb-asset with P3 rwb-case and the platform contract library
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the solution architect and the API contract owner
proposed: Declare RouteRecommendation and the additive route_recommendation property on the two reads of RWB-S5-E3019-CON, publish no operation and no event for the recommendation, and let step D1 decide whether the element is published in the API Specification as a first-class schema.

title: The unit of the expected return, the mapping of the five route words to a closed list and the reason codes are fixed by no source
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E3-027, Acceptance criteria AC1); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.10.2, A2.10.3.1); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T3.1, T3.2, T4); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-DIS-19, R-DIS-21 to R-DIS-26); Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 (DF-SAL-004, DF-SAL-005, DF-ACE-270 to DF-ACE-279)
section: CON s2 Business rationale; s7 AC1 and AC2; s8 BR5, BR6; s9 State transitions; s11 Data; s12.8; s13 Solution plan; s19; APP s2, s7 AC1, s8 BR6, s11 Data
description: The criterion asks for the expected return on each route and R-DIS-19 asks for the reasons and the COLLINS economics, but no source gives a return field, a percentage, a currency rule, a reason code list or a model for the return. The data model gives prices on listing (start_price and floor_price, both numeric with no unit) and a score and estimate on the ACE score row, and the return is therefore declared as an amount with a currency code and the model version of the economics, with the placeholder where a unit is required. The five route words of the criterion have no list: LOV-SALE-CHANNEL carries DUTCH_AUCTION, BROKER, DIRECT, LED_AUCTION and RAMC and no buy-back or rental, while the machine carries ROUTE_APPROVED_BUYBACK and RENTAL_ACTIVE and the R-DIS-21 to R-DIS-26 rows route auction, RAMC, buy-back, rental and broker from ROUTE_WITH_APPROVER. The reasons are declared as coded values because no free-text vocabulary is given and no personal data may enter them.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E3-027 AC1 reads proposes auction, broker, RAMC, buy-back or rental with the expected return on each; TSD S5 v2 T3.1 gives listing start_price and floor_price as numeric(18,2) with no currency column and asset book_value as numeric(18,2), and T3.2 gives LOV-SALE-CHANNEL as DUTCH_AUCTION, BROKER, DIRECT, LED_AUCTION and RAMC with no buy-back and no rental value; T4 gives ROUTE_APPROVED_BUYBACK, RENTAL_ACTIVE, ROUTE_APPROVED_AUCTION and ROUTE_APPROVED_RAMC as states; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 row R-DIS-19 names the reasons and the COLLINS economics without a field, a code or a unit; the ACE score row DF-ACE-270 to DF-ACE-279 gives model_code, model_version, score_value and estimate_value and no return.
area: Data model and contract, S5 rwb-asset with P1 rwb-source-data and P7 rwb-decision
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the data steward and the P7 rwb-decision owner
proposed: Declare the expected return as an amount with a currency code and the model version of the economics, carry the five route words as reference data with their list mapping, declare the reasons as coded values, and let step D1 decide whether a return or reason list is added to reference data.
